translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses with a speaking.
translations.2: Command the sons of Israel that they turn back and encamp before the mouth of the Hiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon — opposite it you shall encamp by the sea.
translations.3: So that Pharaoh will say of the sons of Israel that they are bewildered in the land, and that the open country has been closed upon them.
translations.4: And I shall harden the heart of Pharaoh and he shall pursue them; and I shall make Myself great through Pharaoh and all his host, and the Egyptians shall know that I am God. And so they did.
translations.5: And the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled; and the heart of he and his officers turned against them, and they said: 'What have we done, since we released the sons of Israel from our service?'
translations.6: And he readied his chariot, and took his people with him.
translations.7: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and the rest of the chariots of the Egyptians who were likewise, and officers over all of them.
translations.8: And God hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the sons of Israel — and the sons of Israel were going forth with a raised hand.
translations.9: And the Egyptians pursued them and overtook them encamped by the sea — all the horses of the chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his host — at the mouth of the Hiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
translations.10: And when Pharaoh drew near, the sons of Israel lifted up their eyes — and behold, the Egyptians were journeying after them — and they feared greatly, and they cried out to God.
translations.11: They said to Moses: 'Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you took us to die in the open country? What have you done to us, since you brought us out of Egypt?'
translations.12: Is this not the very word which we said to you in Egypt, saying: Leave us that we may serve the Egyptians — for our service to them is better for us than our death in the open country?'
translations.13: Moses said to the people: 'Do not fear — stand still and behold the salvation of God which He shall work for you today; for as you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall never again see them, forever.'
translations.14: 'God shall fight on your behalf — and as for you, be still.'
translations.15: Then God said to Moses: 'Why do you cry out to Me? Command the sons of Israel that they set out.'
translations.16: 'And you — lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and split it; and the sons of Israel shall enter into the midst of it upon dry land.'
translations.17: 'And I am hardening the heart of the Egyptians, and they shall enter after them; and I shall make Myself great through Pharaoh and all his host and his chariots and his horsemen.'
translations.18: 'And the Egyptians shall know that I am God, when I have made Myself great through Pharaoh, and his chariots, and his horsemen.'
translations.19: And the angel of God, who was going before the camp of the sons of Israel, set out and moved behind them; and the pillar of cloud set out from before them and stood behind them.
translations.20: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of the Israelites; and there were the cloud and the darkness — yet it lit up the night — and neither one drew near the other throughout the night.
translations.21: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and God drove the sea back with a strong qibla-wind throughout the night, until He made it dry, after the water had split apart.
translations.22: And the sons of Israel entered into the midst of the sea upon dry land; and the water was walls for them, on their right and on their left.
translations.23: And the Egyptians pursued them and entered after them — all the horses of Pharaoh, and his chariots and his horsemen — into the midst of the sea.
translations.24: And when it was at the turn of the morning watch, God looked out over the camp of the Egyptians through a pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw it into confusion.
translations.25: And He removed the wheels of their chariots and drove them with force, so that the Egyptians said: 'Let us flee from before the sons of Israel, for God is fighting against the Egyptians on their behalf.'
translations.26: And God said to Moses: 'Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the water may return upon the Egyptians, and upon their chariots and their horsemen.'
translations.27: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and it returned, at the approach of morning, to its strength — while they were fleeing toward it — and God drowned them in its midst.
translations.28: In that the water returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, and the rest of the hosts of Pharaoh who had entered after them into the sea — there did not remain among them even one.
translations.29: And the sons of Israel walked upon the dry land in the midst of the sea; and the water was walls for them, on their right and on their left.
translations.30: And God saved, on that day, the sons of Israel from the hand of the Egyptians; and the sons of Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the shore of the sea.
translations.31: And the sons of Israel saw the great plague which God had brought upon the Egyptians; and the people feared God, and believed in God and in Moses His messenger.
